memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'But you must keep my decrees and my laws. The native-born and the foreigners residing among you must not do any of these detestable things, for all these things were done by the people who lived in the land before you, and the land became defiled.'" - Lev 18:26-27 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The native-born and the foreigners residing among you. The same standard for everyone living in the land.

We have met this phrase repeatedly in Leviticus, and it keeps saying the same thing: God does not run two systems. There is no arrangement where insiders are held to one standard and outsiders to another, or where the well-connected are quietly exempt.

That is rarer than it should be. Most human institutions develop unwritten exceptions — for the powerful, the useful, the ones we cannot afford to lose. Churches are not immune. A gifted leader is protected while an ordinary member is disciplined. A generous giver is handled carefully. We do not intend it. It simply happens.

James saw it happening in the first century and named it as sin. If you show favouritism, you sin and are convicted by the law as lawbreakers (Jas 2:9).

God's household does not work this way. There is one standard, applied evenly, because there is one God who shows no partiality.

That should reassure anyone who has ever been on the wrong side of an unwritten exception. God will not treat you as less. And it should sober anyone who has benefited from one.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you seen unwritten exceptions made for certain people?
2. Have you ever benefited from being treated as an exception?
3. What would even-handedness look like in your church or workplace?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You show no favouritism and hold everyone to the same standard. Search my heart for partiality, and make me fair in how I treat others. Amen.
